A patch release that renames the environment variables from `EV_` to `FD_`. Existing deployments keep working unchanged.

## Changed

- **`FD_` environment variables.** Every setting that was an `EV_` variable is now documented and read under `FD_`: `FD_CONFIG`, `FD_PROVIDER`, `FD_REPOS`, `FD_TOKEN`, `FD_BASE_URL`, `FD_SUB_ISSUES`, `FD_ORDERING_MODE`, `FD_VIEW_ID`, `FD_VIEW_TITLE`, `FD_PRIORITY_LABELS`, `FD_HOST`, `FD_PORT`, `FD_CACHE_TTL`, `FD_REFRESH_MINUTES`, `FD_BASIC_AUTH` and `FD_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. The image sets `FD_HOST` and `FD_PORT`.
- **The old names still work.** An `EV_` variable that is set still applies and still wins over its `FD_` counterpart, so nothing changes until you rename. Startup and `forge-desk check` print a warning for each one, naming its `FD_` replacement. The `EV_` names are removed in the next major release.
- **Release Compose file.** `docker-compose.release.yml` reads `FD_IMAGE` and `FD_BASIC_AUTH`. It stops with a message while only `EV_IMAGE` is set.

## Upgrading from 3.0.0

Nothing has to change now. To move to the new names, rename each variable in `.env` and in your compose file's `environment:` lines in one step. Compose passes the container only the names listed there, so a `FD_BASIC_AUTH` that is set in `.env` but not listed never reaches the app, and the app then starts without its login. Variable names you chose yourself in `tokenEnv`, `passwordEnv` or `secretEnv` are read as written. Afterwards, `forge-desk check` should print no `is deprecated` warning. Details: [docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](https://github.com/brunoorsolon/forge-desk/blob/main/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md#upgrading).
